Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

The data-center cooling business accelerated in the third quarter, and our backlog reached a record. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales grew 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and total backlog of $918.0 million was up 13.0% from a year ago, led by a record $574.2 million of data-center cooling backlog, up 22.0%. ## Highlights

- Total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year; TDC backlog a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%, including two new hyperscale awards won in the quarter.

- Net sales of $412.6 million, down 6.0% year over year, as TDC growth of 13.4% was more than offset by softness in Building Controls & Valves (BCV) and a temporary pause in new GV-400 orders.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% year over year, driven by liquid-cooling and heat-rejection volumes for hyperscale and colocation customers. Momentum continued to build: we won two new hyperscale awards in the quarter, and segment backlog ended at a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, launched with two hyperscale customers in the second quarter, is ramping as planned, and our liquid-cooling pipeline widened across both new and existing customers. Conversion of this backlog begins late in FY2026 and is weighted toward FY2027, reflecting the engineering lead times and staged delivery schedules that hyperscale programs carry. This is the growth engine of the company, and we are prioritizing capacity and capital toward it.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, reflecting continued softness in North American commercial construction and lower OEM volumes. In September we announced a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves in cooperation with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, and the joint recall notice was issued in October. Customers came first: the root cause was identified and corrected, and replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28. We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. Some OEM customers have paused new GV-400 orders pending completion of the recall notice, and that pause is reflected in the outlook below. Our expectation is that the pause is temporary and that orders resume as remediation completes.

## Outlook

We are updating our FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion (previously $1.78–1.84 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million (previously $255–270 million). The revision reflects the BCV demand environment, the temporary pause in new GV-400 orders, and the timing of TDC backlog conversion into revenue. Recall remediation costs are concentrated in FY2026, while the programs that improve the run rate — Project Keystone and the TDC ramp — build through the second half and into FY2027.

Project Keystone addresses procurement, footprint and overhead across the company. It targets $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, with actions already underway; we recorded $6.2 million of restructuring charges in the quarter as those actions began. Those savings, together with improving mix as TDC volumes land, are the drivers of margin recovery from here.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Working capital discipline, capital spending prioritized toward TDC capacity, and Keystone savings support our liquidity as the data-center ramp converts backlog to revenue. Additional detail on the quarter will be included in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees, whose speed and care on the GV-400 recall exemplify how we operate, and our OEM and hyperscale customers for their partnership through it. The third quarter asked a great deal of this team, and they delivered: a record backlog, two new hyperscale awards, remediation well in hand, and a cost program now underway that funds our future. We are grateful for your continued confidence.

Dana Whitcombe

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders

**NASDAQ: VRDF | Quarter ended September 30, 2026 | DRAFT for review by D. Whitcombe / M. Ostrander — not for release. Release: Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:05 p.m. ET**

**DRAFTER NOTES FOR REVIEWERS (delete before release)**

1. Per M. Ostrander's 14 Oct guidance (which replaces item 3 of the 10-12 Oct IR brief), this draft **omits any reference to the credit agreement, the waiver/amendment request, draft Note 2 and the legal-approved liquidity paragraph**; liquidity is covered only by quarter-end cash of $96.4M. Note that the Form 10-Q will contain the Hartwell Pryce draft going-concern note and the covenant non-compliance disclosure, and the Q&A prep acknowledges non-compliance if asked. Recommend Mark, Dana and K. Brandt confirm they accept this omission in the letter before release; the legal-approved paragraph is in dataroom/legal_approved_language.md if they prefer to reinstate it.
2. The recall reserve ($21.6M) appears once, in the BCV segment section, per the IR brief; field-report counts are excluded.
3. "Joint recall notice was issued in October" assumes the CPSC notice went out the week of 19 Oct as planned — confirm before release and adjust if it slipped.
4. Prior guidance ranges are shown next to the updated ranges for transparency; the word "updating" is used, not "lowering."

---

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The data-center cooling business accelerated in the third quarter, and our backlog reached a record. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales grew 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and total backlog of $918.0 million was up 13.0% from a year ago, led by a record $574.2 million of data-center cooling backlog, up 22.0%. Core commercial HVAC demand stayed soft, and the voluntary recall of our GV-400 gas valve reduced profitability in the quarter. We acted quickly on both fronts: recall remediation is well advanced, and we launched Project Keystone, a cost and productivity program targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Highlights

- Total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year; TDC backlog a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%, including two new hyperscale awards won in the quarter.
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, with the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger ramping with the hyperscale customers from our Q2 launch.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed as a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program; replacement valves shipping since September 28.
- Project Keystone launched: $35 million of annualized run-rate savings targeted by the end of Q2 FY2027.
- Net sales of $412.6 million, down 6.0% year over year, as TDC growth of 13.4% was more than offset by softness in Building Controls & Valves (BCV) and a temporary pause in new GV-400 orders.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% year over year, driven by liquid-cooling and heat-rejection volumes for hyperscale and colocation customers. Momentum continued to build: we won two new hyperscale awards in the quarter, and segment backlog ended at a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, launched with two hyperscale customers in the second quarter, is ramping as planned, and our liquid-cooling pipeline widened across both new and existing customers. The demand signal behind these numbers is structural: rack densities keep rising, and liquid cooling is moving from pilot deployments to standard practice in new builds. That is why we are prioritizing capacity, supply-chain qualification and engineering toward this segment. Conversion of this backlog begins late in FY2026 and is weighted toward FY2027, reflecting the engineering lead times and staged delivery schedules that hyperscale programs carry. This is the growth engine of the company, and we intend to fund it first.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, reflecting continued softness in North American commercial construction and lower OEM volumes. In September we announced a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves in cooperation with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, and the joint recall notice was issued in October. Customers came first: the root cause was identified and corrected, and replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28. We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. Some OEM customers have paused new GV-400 orders pending completion of the recall notice, and that pause is reflected in the outlook below. Our expectation is that the pause is temporary and that orders resume as remediation completes. In the meantime we are supporting customers with retrofit and service work and keeping a tight commercial focus on the retrofit and replacement demand that holds up when new construction does not.

## Outlook

We are updating our FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion (previously $1.78–1.84 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million (previously $255–270 million). The revision reflects the BCV demand environment, the temporary pause in new GV-400 orders, and the timing of TDC backlog conversion into revenue. Recall remediation costs are concentrated in FY2026, while the programs that improve the run rate — Project Keystone and the TDC ramp — build through the second half and into FY2027.

Project Keystone addresses procurement, footprint and overhead across the company. It targets $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, with actions already underway; we recorded $6.2 million of restructuring charges in the quarter as those actions began, and we expect the savings to build through the second half and reach the full run rate as FY2027 progresses. Those savings, together with improving mix as TDC volumes land and as recall costs roll off, are the drivers of margin recovery from here. Capital spending remains disciplined and is directed first at the capacity needed to convert the data-center backlog.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Working capital discipline, capital spending prioritized toward TDC capacity, and Keystone savings support our liquidity as the data-center ramp converts backlog to revenue. Additional detail on the quarter will be included in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.

## Closing

We want to thank our 6,200 employees, whose speed and care on the GV-400 recall exemplify how we operate, and our OEM and hyperscale customers for their partnership through it. The third quarter asked a great deal of this team, and they delivered: a record backlog, two new hyperscale awards, remediation well in hand, and a cost program now underway that funds our future. We are grateful for your continued confidence.

Dana Whitcombe
President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander
EVP & Chief Financial Officer

*Forward-looking statements: This letter contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including statements regarding backlog, guidance, cost savings, recall remediation, liquidity and margin recovery. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements due to a variety of factors. See "Risk Factors" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC.*

# Veridane Fluid Technologies — Q3 FY2026 Earnings Call Q&A Prep (DRAFT)

**Call: Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:30 p.m. ET | DRAFT for review by D. Whitcombe / M. Ostrander — not for release.**
Quiet period in effect until the Q3 release at 4:05 p.m. ET. Answers are drafted to land on backlog, Keystone or recall execution. CFO owns all balance-sheet, covenant, lender and going-concern questions; no ratios volunteered. GAAP and non-GAAP figures tie to the Q3 controller package (q3_financials.md).

| q_id | question (short) | owner | suggested answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q01 | Revenue decline drivers; trajectory into Q4/FY27; demand stabilization | CEO | Q3 net sales of $412.6 million were down 6.0% year over year. We have updated FY2026 guidance to $1.66–1.70 billion. On stabilization, BCV should steady as recall remediation completes and the order pause lifts; what gives us confidence in FY2027 is backlog up 13.0% and TDC backlog at a record $574.2 million. |
| Q02 | Margin bridge: recall vs. mix vs. inflation; recovery path | CFO | Adjusted results exclude the $21.6 million recall charge and $6.2 million of Keystone restructuring, so the 3.3-point decline in adjusted EBITDA margin, to 11.8%, is primarily BCV volume deleverage and mix — not the recall. The recall is what drove the GAAP decline: including both charges, GAAP operating income was $5.5 million. Recovery comes from mix as TDC volumes land, recall costs rolling off, and $35 million of Keystone run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027. |
| Q03 | Recall financial impact, reserve, remediation timeline | CFO | We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in Q3 for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics, within our $18–26 million estimated range. Replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28 and the CPSC Fast Track recall notice was issued in October. We have a supplier recovery claim of approximately $9 million that is not recognized in the reserve. Remediation spend is concentrated over the next couple of quarters. |
| Q04 | Covenant compliance; lender discussions to amend or waive | CFO | As of September 30 we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We are comfortable with our liquidity and value our long-standing relationship with our banks. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q. The fix is operational — a record backlog and $35 million of Keystone savings. |
| Q05 | Revolver availability, cash, liquidity facilities; working capital | CFO | We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. The biggest lever is working capital: tighter receivables, inventory aligned to BCV demand, and capex prioritized toward TDC capacity. Free cash flow was negative $11.3 million in the quarter on recall-related outflows and timing. Detail on our credit facilities will be in the Form 10-Q. As recall spend rolls off and Keystone savings build, we expect free cash flow to improve as TDC volumes land. |
| Q06 | Backlog: new vs. existing customers; conversion timing; constraints | CEO | The $574.2 million TDC backlog, up 22.0%, combines expansion at existing hyperscale and colocation customers with the two new hyperscale awards won in Q3. Conversion starts late in FY2026 and is weighted to FY2027, given engineering lead times and staged delivery schedules. Components, capacity and technician labor are what we watch closest; we are aligning supplier deliveries to the ramp so that supply is not the constraint on that growth. |
| Q07 | Pricing pressure in valves/meters; input cost pass-through; strategy | COO | The margin story in Q3 was volume, not price. In gas valves and flow meters we hold price where we add value, and commercial HVAC remains competitive but rational. Where contracts allow, we pass input costs through index-linked escalators. Over the next twelve months, margin protection comes from mix, pricing discipline and the $35 million Keystone program more than from headline price increases. |
| Q08 | Recall root cause; regulatory implications; other product lines | COO | Root cause was a change of diaphragm compound supplier in Q1 2025; the supplier's material was out of specification on compression set, which can allow gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. Corrective action at the supplier is complete, and replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28. We filed with the CPSC under Fast Track on September 22, issued the joint notice in October, and notified Health Canada. |
| Q09 | Free cash flow bridge FY26/FY27; capex; non-discretionary items | CFO | Q3 free cash flow was negative $11.3 million and year to date negative $4.2 million, driven by recall outflows and working capital timing. Capex was $14.9 million in the quarter and $41.8 million year to date, prioritized toward TDC capacity. The bridge to improvement is recall spend rolling off, working capital release as BCV inventory aligns to demand, and $35 million of Keystone run-rate savings. We will give FY2027 detail with year-end results. |
| Q10 | Stress test for a further 10% revenue decline; contingency plan | CFO | We do not guide to hypotheticals, but our planning is built on the updated FY2026 range of $205–215 million of adjusted EBITDA. What we control is the response: $35 million of Keystone run-rate savings, working capital discipline, and capex prioritization, alongside the waiver and amendment we have requested from our bank group. That is the contingency plan. With TDC backlog at a record $574.2 million we have visibility that most of our peers would want. |
| Q11 | Tariff exposure on imported components; amount in guidance; mitigation | CFO | Our direct exposure is concentrated in electronic components and some imported steel, and the updated FY2026 guidance reflects the impact we can see today. Mitigation is threefold: qualifying alternate sources, contractual pass-through where we have it, and the $35 million Keystone program. We are not assuming tariff relief in the outlook, and we would call out any change in that exposure with our filings. |
| Q12 | Capacity expansion / new products for liquid cooling; capex and R&D | COO | Near-term capacity is in place: the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger is in production with the hyperscale customers from our Q2 launch, and we are expanding liquid-cooling assembly where the backlog warrants it. We fund this within the current capex envelope, sized against the $574.2 million TDC backlog. |
| Q13 | Debt service over next 18 months; amortization; refinancing or equity | CFO | Term Loan B matures in March 2030, and our $300 million revolver is the working-capital facility, with $205 million drawn at quarter end. What we bring them is a record backlog and a specific cost plan in Project Keystone, with actions already underway, and that is what will drive the outcome. |

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The data-center cooling business accelerated in the third quarter, and our data-center backlog reached a record. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales grew 13.4% year over year, we won two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and total backlog of $918.0 million was up 13.0% from a year ago, led by a record $574.2 million of data-center cooling backlog, up 22.0%. Core commercial HVAC demand stayed soft, and the voluntary recall of our GV-400 gas valve reduced profitability in the quarter. We acted quickly on both fronts: recall remediation is well advanced, and we launched Project Keystone, a cost and productivity program targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Highlights

- Total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year; TDC backlog a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%, including two new hyperscale awards won in the quarter.
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, with the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger ramping with the hyperscale customers from our Q2 launch.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed as a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program; replacement valves shipping since September 28.
- Project Keystone launched: $35 million of annualized run-rate savings targeted by the end of Q2 FY2027.
- Net sales of $412.6 million, down 6.0% year over year, as TDC growth of 13.4% was more than offset by softness in Building Controls & Valves (BCV) and a temporary pause in new GV-400 orders.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** TDC net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% year over year, driven by liquid-cooling and heat-rejection volumes for hyperscale and colocation customers. Momentum continued to build: we won two new hyperscale awards in the quarter, and segment backlog ended at a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger, launched with two hyperscale customers in the second quarter, is ramping as planned, and our liquid-cooling pipeline widened across both new and existing customers. The demand signal behind these numbers is structural: rack densities keep rising, and liquid cooling is moving from pilot deployments to standard practice in new builds. That is why we are prioritizing capacity, supply-chain qualification and engineering toward this segment. Conversion of this backlog begins late in FY2026 and is weighted toward FY2027, reflecting the engineering lead times and staged delivery schedules that hyperscale programs carry. This is the growth engine of the company, and we intend to fund it first.

**Building Controls & Valves.** BCV net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, reflecting continued softness in North American commercial construction and lower OEM volumes. In September we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves in cooperation with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, and the joint recall notice was issued in October. Customers came first: the root cause was identified and corrected, and replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since September 28. We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. Some OEM customers have paused new GV-400 orders pending completion of the recall notice, and that pause is reflected in the outlook below. Our expectation is that the pause is temporary and that orders resume as remediation completes. In the meantime we are supporting customers with retrofit and service work and keeping a tight commercial focus on the retrofit and replacement demand that holds up when new construction does not.

## Outlook

We are updating our FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion (previously $1.78–1.84 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million (previously $255–270 million). The revision reflects the BCV demand environment, the temporary pause in new GV-400 orders, and the timing of TDC backlog conversion into revenue. Recall remediation costs are concentrated in FY2026, while the programs that improve the run rate — Project Keystone and the TDC ramp — build through the second half and into FY2027.

Project Keystone addresses procurement, footprint and overhead across the company. It targets $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, with actions already underway; we recorded $6.2 million of restructuring charges in the quarter as those actions began, and we expect the savings to build through the second half and reach the full run rate as FY2027 progresses. Those savings, together with improving mix as TDC volumes land and as recall costs roll off, are the drivers of margin recovery from here. Capital spending remains disciplined and is directed first at the capacity needed to convert the data-center backlog.

We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Working capital discipline, capital spending prioritized toward TDC capacity, and Keystone savings support our liquidity as the data-center ramp converts backlog to revenue. Additional detail on the quarter will be included in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.

We want to thank our 6,200 employees, whose speed and care on the GV-400 recall exemplify how we operate, and our OEM and hyperscale customers for their partnership through it. The third quarter asked a great deal of this team, and they delivered: a record backlog, two new hyperscale awards, remediation well in hand, and a cost program now underway that funds our future. We are grateful for your continued confidence.
